cells.tense: The piece is finished, and you are sitting with what you learned finishing it.
cells.act: rest in the connection without doing anything with it
cells.ask: With one person who had a hand in this, spend an hour with nothing to do — no fixing, no rehashing, no next. Say nothing about what's done unless it comes up. Time has no say here; the hour is only a shape.
cells.core:
You have gone about as deep as a person can go into your own thinking, and you are still here, finishing something. There is a way this goes well: the pattern holds, you've tested it against everything you've got, and it settles into a conclusion you can rest in rather than defend. Something is complete, and instead of it closing on you, it opens into what you've come to understand.

The quiet after finishing is not empty, and you're letting it stay that way. What keeps this is simple: give the settled understanding some time with the person it's about, with nothing asked of them. That's all it is. An hour with nothing to do, and the stable feeling that follows understanding belongs to nobody else once you've stopped handling it.
cells.sheetLine: Finished, and what you learned is still sitting with you.
cells.verb: going so deep into the pattern that thinking meets its own floor
cells.place: where something is finished and the next thing has not started

cells.tense: You will hand over the finished thing before it has actually finished itself.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Open the next conversation about this work by naming its frame yourself — what it covers and what it leaves out — before any question is asked. One sentence, said first. Then let the conversation go where it goes.
cells.core:
The thinking has an end, and you are about to be past it — waiting for the last page to give you permission will put you in the wrong building. Today the conclusion gets carried out early. Yet what's actually there gets harder to say plainly the longer it sits unspoken, and the people waiting on it can feel something coming that hasn't been put down yet.

Give the frame a voice before anyone else gives it one. Open the next conversation by naming what this covers and what it leaves out, first, in one sentence, then stop. That is the whole act, and it doesn't need the work to be done. It puts an edge on what you see, and it usually arrives before the last page does.

cells.tense: The last thing you completed stays finished, and nothing has been marked since.
cells.act: let the gladness go out to the room
cells.ask: Think of one thing you carried to the end lately. Across a week or so, whenever it crosses your mind, register whether any gladness moves toward other people. Don't make any, don't act on it, and don't decide what it means.
cells.core:
There's a landing you keep hovering. The last thing went as far as it goes and then you stopped at the top of the stairs — not finishing the finishing, and not saying so either. The depth is still good; the trouble is it goes out to nobody, so nothing comes back, and the next thing starts from lower than it should.

So don't try to feel more about it. Watch instead: when a finished thing crosses your mind, register whether any gladness reaches toward anyone else. Don't push it, don't perform it, don't do anything with what you find. That reaching is how completing lands, and it's worth knowing where your edge sits.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped marking finishes, so the next one starts lower.

cells.tense: The integration is happening in your hands, and you are calling it something else.
cells.act: spend an hour with the thing you love without a task attached to it
cells.ask: Name one person you have just brought something to its end with. Make a standing practice: a stretch of time together with no task, no fixing, no reviewing. No clock, no end plan. Keep it going a few weeks, deciding nothing about it.
cells.core:
The tying-off is happening — holding the threads of what is nearly done, seeing how it fits, deciding what can be let go — and if someone asked, you'd say the calm after finishing is just how things are. It isn't. The quiet that follows completion is work that has gone quiet, and the picture of who did it has lost your name.

Go simpler than the question of who did it. Make a standing habit with the person you've just taken a thing to the end with: time together with no task, no fixing, no reviewing, no clock. It sets when you stop handling it, and afterwards nothing has to be called anything. What you know of them stays yours; what they know stays theirs.
cells.sheetLine: The calm after finishing is your own work, quiet.
